description: Single and two storey side extension; rear dormer; one rooflight in front roof slope; external alterations
decision_conditions:
<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="">The proposed two storey side extension,
in conjunction with the proposed dormer, by reason of inappropriate design,
cumulative excessive bulk and massing would result in an unduly obtrusive and
incongruous addition that would poorly relate to the existing dwelling detracting
from the character of the host property, the terrace in which it sits and
properties in the surrounding area. The development is contrary to the high
quality design aspirations set out in The National Planning Policy Framework
(2024), policies D3 (D(1) and D(11)) of The London Plan (2021), Policy CS1.B on
the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), Policy DM1 of the Development Management Local
Plans Policies (2013) and Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design
Guide (2010).<font face="PT Sans, sans-serif"><o:p></o:p></font></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="">The proposal, by reason of the site
being located within an area of land liable to flooding and the lack of a
comprehensive Flood Risk Assessment, due to a lack of flood data, flood mitigation measures which
take into account the depth of the flood, and compensatory flood storage
details, has failed to demonstrate that the proposed development would not
exacerbate the risk of flooding within the site or increase the risk and
consequences of flooding elsewhere, contrary to the National Planning Policy
Framework (2024), Policy SI12 and SI13 of The London Plan (2021), Core Policy CS1.U
of Harrow Core Strategy (2012) and Policies DM9 and DM10 of the Harrow
Development Management Polices Local Plan (2013).<font face="PT Sans, sans-serif"><o:p></o:p></font></p>

<p>Due
to its siting, proximity to the boundaries, bulk, scale, height and massing,
the proposed two storey side extension and rear dormer would result in undue overbearing and visual impacts to the gardens of Nos. 80
and 82 Cecil Road, to the detriment of the amenities of those neighbouring occupiers.&nbsp; As such, the proposal is contrary to the National Planning
Policy Framework (2024), Policies D3.D(7) of The London Plan (2021), Policy CS1
of the Harrow Core Strategy (2013), policy DM1 of the Harrow Development
Management Policies Local Plan (2013) and the adopted Supplementary Planning
Document: Residential Design Guide Supplementary Planning Document (2010).</p>
